pdf_explanation: When the object on the left is turned upside down you get the object on right.
why: The hat in figure 1 is upside down; in figure 2 it is turned the right way up, so the picture is flipped top to bottom. Flip figure 3 top to bottom the same way: the long bar goes to the top, the two small blocks go to the bottom, and the white side faces now slope downwards. That is option 1. Option 4 is tempting, but it is flipped left to right (the white faces moved to the left side), not upside down.
trick: When figure 1 to figure 2 is a flip, check which edge moved: top-bottom flip keeps left and right the same. Follow one small detail, like a white side face, to tell flips apart.
note: PDF answer A matches the upside-down (top-bottom flip) rule; A is an exact vertical mirror of figure 3.
